price_scope: Chips for own PCB; shipping, front-end amplifiers/buffers, references/clock, board and assembly excluded. Price and stock observations are not reservations.

adc_necessity.answer: Analog load-cell bridges and the analog ADXL354 outputs must be converted to digital numbers for this digital controller. An ADC is therefore necessary somewhere; a separate ADC chip is optional if an MCU or digital sensor/amplifier supplies a suitable acquisition chain.
adc_necessity.assumption: A proper instrumentation amplifier, suitable buffering and a chosen analog cutoff are allowed. Their noise, offset, gain, input range, settling and phase are still real parts of the chain.
adc_necessity.current_loop: The force ADC chain does not establish the 50 microsecond coil-current response. Use a separate sufficiently fast current measurement/control loop. All eight M08 channels are already allocated in the six-bridge plus two-acceleration-axis configuration.

parts.technical_basis: Tables 7-1/7-2 and Digital Filter section. Eight simultaneous differential inputs. Maximum specified rate 32 ks/s per channel. Gain-one RMS noise at OSR128 is 21.31 microvolts. At external 7.68MHz clock, modulator 3.84MHz, OSR128 gives 30ks/s. Use the OSR128 noise value without claiming improvement from the clock reduction.
parts.role: Conditional default when six raw bridge channels and two acceleration axes must be acquired together.

parts.technical_basis: Table 7-1 OSR128 gain-one noise is also 21.31 microvolts RMS; same sinc3 topology at that OSR. Its higher advertised 64ks/s setting has higher noise and is not this comparison.
parts.role: Lower-cost plausible planar four-channel route: two independent force channels plus two acceleration axes. Assumes the chosen load cell actually exposes only the necessary independent channels. No complete hardware chain has been qualified.

parts.technical_basis: Table 7-1 also lists 21.31 microvolts RMS at OSR128 gain1. Six simultaneous differential channels.
parts.role: Conditional six-channel route, for example three independent force channels plus three acceleration axes. Three-dimensional force estimation is outside the present planar qualification model.

Two channels alone cannot accommodate the present two-force plus two-acceleration planar chain. Two M02 chips cost more than one M04 and need shared clock/reset and verified inter-device timing. The M02 full transfer/noise sheet was not reviewed for this study; no equivalence claim is made.

parts.technical_basis: 100ks/s maximum aggregate at 5V, 50ks/s at 2.7V. One multiplexed SAR. With eight channels, at most 12.5ks/s each at the 5V aggregate limit, and readings are time-separated. MCP3208-C INL up to +/-2LSB, offset +/-3LSB, gain +/-5LSB; these are not removed by simple averaging.
parts.role: Cheap single-channel or slow acquisition part. The present diagnostic's 12-bit quantization-only envelope does not qualify this chip: its timing, mux settling, input range, INL and channel skew differ.

parts.technical_basis: Two native 12-bit SAR ADC cores, up to 4Msps at full resolution. Table63 maximum-speed single-ADC characterization lists approximately 10.6bits typical single-ended ENOB (10bits minimum), and about 10.9 differential. Those values apply to stated high-rate conditions, not a guarantee for an oversampled implementation.
parts.role: Potentially no extra ADC chip. Needs its own complete synchronization, oversampling/filter, reference, input settling and measured noise/INL qualification. The ideal 12-bit spacing test is not an STM32 ADC test.
Popular low-cost 16-bit part whose rate/filter cannot support the present 10kHz/controller and 1.64kHz cell correction. No simulation or price comparison is needed to identify this incompatibility.

conversion_scale_assumptions.note: A 12g ADC full scale does not increase the physical accelerometer's +/-8g range. Instrumentation gain can use more converter span, subject to actual raw loads and overload headroom.

report_conclusions: Separate chip necessity and conversion necessity are different questions.
A slower setting on the same M08 chip does not reduce its purchase cost; it reduces noise at the expense of extra filtering delay.
Saving by reducing unnecessary channel count can preserve stated per-channel ADC performance; reducing required force directions is a separate mechanical/sensing decision.
The cheapest globally qualified ADC is not established because the full fixed-mechanics controller already fails the force target at its reference acquisition.
Nominal code count, RMS noise, calibrated accuracy, latency and bandwidth must be reported separately.
